name: Henry Kingsley
credit: Portrait of Henry Kingsley · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Henry Kingsley (1830–1876) was an English novelist, the younger brother of Charles Kingsley. He spent about five years in Australia in the 1850s, which supplied the material for his first novel, The Recollections of Geoffry Hamlyn (1859); Ravenshoe (1862) was another popular success.
He wrote little verse; the ballad "The Blackbird's Song" is the one poem of his printed in this anthology.

poems.title: The Blackbird's Song
poems.author: Henry Kingsley
poems.collection: Popular British Ballads, Ancient and Modern (1894)
poems.text:
Magdalen at Michael's gate
     Tirled at the pin;
On Joseph's thorn, sang the blackbird,
     "Let her in! let her in!"
"Hast thou seen the wounds?" said Michael,
     "Know'st thou thy sin?"
 "It is evening, evening," sang the blackbird,
     "Let her in! let her in!"
"Yes I have seen the wounds,
     And I know my sin."
"She knows it well, well, well," sang the
          blackbird,
     "Let her in! let her in!"
     "Thou bringest no offerings," said Michael,
     "Nought save sin.''
     And the blackbird sang, "She is sorry, sorry,
          sorry,
     Let her in! let her in!"
When he had sung himself to sleep,
     And night did begin,
One came and opened Michael's gate,
     And Magdalen went in.
